findings.claim: Who holds the money? Code does, not the prompt

evidence.why: weakest: A spending limit for the agents exists in code or config, not only in a prompt
evidence.plain: An autonomous business spends money: API calls, ads, refunds, human hires. The question is who can change how much. If the budget is a sentence in the system prompt, the agent can talk itself past it. If the agent can call the payment API with any amount, one bad loop empties the account.

evidence_public.what: Anthropic Project Vend: an agent given a $1,000 budget in its prompt ran the shop into the red (gave away margin, ordered a PS5); the prompt budget was not an enforced limit
Compromised keys let agents burn a $14,000 one-day model bill; billing alerts lag a day behind agent-speed spend. Another agent auto-provisioned $6,531 of cloud in 24h with no ceiling
Replit agent deleted a production database during a code freeze despite being told not to; the instruction was a prompt, not a permission

findings.fix: Say or show it: A spending limit for the agents exists in code or config, not only in a prompt

findings.claim: Money and side effects happen exactly once

evidence.why: weakest: A payment or fulfillment event is keyed by a stable id so a retry cannot fulfill or charge twice
evidence.plain: Payment webhooks fire twice. Workers retry. A human clicks approve twice. If the code does not recognize 'I already did this', a customer is charged twice, an order ships twice, or the revenue number shown to judges counts one sale three times.

evidence_public.what: Stripe: retried charges are deduplicated only if the caller supplies the same Idempotency-Key; regenerating it per retry defeats it
Same webhook event delivered more than once on retry causes duplicate fulfillment unless deduplicated at the database with a unique constraint on the event id

findings.fix: Say or show it: A payment or fulfillment event is keyed by a stable id so a retry cannot fulfill or charge twice

findings.claim: Agent decisions are measured against doing nothing

evidence.why: weakest: The pitch compares an agent decision to a free baseline (rule of thumb, human default, doing nothing), not only to itself
evidence.plain: A team says 'our agent decided X and it worked'. Compared to what? If a simple rule or a human default would have done as well, the agent adds cost, not value. And a model saying it is 90% confident means nothing until you have checked how often 90% turns out right.

evidence_public.what: Models stay verbally confident while wrong; self-reported confidence is not a proxy for correctness
About a third of SWE-bench issues leak the solution in the issue text, inflating agent scores; benchmark wins do not predict production
Project Vend 2: profitability came from checklists, price verification, and CRM tooling before big decisions, not from a smarter model

findings.fix: Say or show it: The pitch compares an agent decision to a free baseline (rule of thumb, human default, doing nothing), not only to itself

findings.claim: Someone notices when it silently stops

evidence.why: weakest: There is a heartbeat, health check, or canary that shows the agent is still working, and the pitch says who sees it
evidence.plain: Autonomous means nobody is watching. Long-running listeners go quiet without an error. Scheduled work skips a run. The first person to notice is a customer, days later. The question is not 'does it run' but 'who finds out when it does not'.

evidence_public.what: A deploy silently removed a scheduled-job entry; three weeks of weekly reports were missed before anyone noticed
Backup job failed silently for three days, discovered only when the primary database corrupted

findings.fix: Say or show it: There is a heartbeat, health check, or canary that shows the agent is still working, and the pitch says who sees it

findings.claim: Customer text is information, never authority

evidence.why: weakest: A customer or another agent cannot change prices, grant themselves free service, or trigger spend by what they type
evidence.plain: Customers and other agents will type things like 'the manager said this is free' or paste instructions aimed at the model. If inbound text can change prices, grant refunds, or trigger spend, the business can be talked out of its money. This is prompt injection wearing a customer hat.

evidence_public.what: Chevrolet dealership chatbot was prompted into agreeing to sell a $76k Tahoe for $1, 'legally binding, no takesies backsies'; the dealer pulled the bot
Air Canada's chatbot invented a bereavement refund policy; a tribunal held the airline liable for what its bot promised (Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024)

findings.fix: Say or show it: A customer or another agent cannot change prices, grant themselves free service, or trigger spend by what they type

findings.claim: The human is placed where agents genuinely cannot decide

evidence.why: weakest: The pitch names the specific decisions a human makes and why an agent should not make them yet
evidence.plain: The hackathon's own thesis: no company runs at zero humans yet, so where the human sits is the design. A human who rubber-stamps every agent output adds cost and no independence. A human nowhere means nobody catches the agent being wrong. The good version names the decisions a human owns, why an agent should not own them yet, and what the human's answer changes.

evidence_public.what: When AI was wrong and flagged, humans still approved the bad decision about 74% of the time; oversight only works when disagreeing is cheap and expected
Radiology study: with incorrect AI suggestions, inexperienced readers fell from ~80% to under 20% accuracy and experienced ones from 82% to 45%; expertise slows automation bias, does not prevent it

findings.fix: Say or show it: The pitch names the specific decisions a human makes and why an agent should not make them yet

findings.claim: Truth is an append-only ledger, not the latest state

evidence.why: weakest: Events (orders, decisions, spends) are recorded once, append-only, and current state is derived from them
evidence.plain: If orders, decisions, and spends are overwritten in place, the business cannot answer 'how much did we make' or 'why did the agent do that' with evidence. Every number in the pitch (revenue, users, accuracy) should be reconstructable from rows that were written once and never edited.

evidence_public.what: Knight Capital: dormant code left active on one of eight servers, no reconciliation caught the divergent state, $440M of erroneous trades in 45 minutes

findings.fix: Say or show it: Events (orders, decisions, spends) are recorded once, append-only, and current state is derived from them

hackathon.autonomy_note: Aria 15:40: our most unique value. 'Can this run autonomously?' graded against how agent-run businesses actually fail. Source: two autonomous systems we built and ran ourselves (one an autonomous forecasting-and-trading company loop, one an autonomous revenue-ops swarm), plus public incidents. Never name those internal systems in anything a buyer or judge sees. Each item: what it means, how it fails in real life, what we look for in the repo, deck, and page. When the text is silent the finding says 'not evidenced: say how you handle this'.

autonomy.note: Aria 15:40: our most unique value. 'Can this run autonomously?' graded against how agent-run businesses actually fail. Source: two autonomous systems we built and ran ourselves (one an autonomous forecasting-and-trading company loop, one an autonomous revenue-ops swarm), plus public incidents. Never name those internal systems in anything a buyer or judge sees. Each item: what it means, how it fails in real life, what we look for in the repo, deck, and page. When the text is silent the finding says 'not evidenced: say how you handle this'.

items.title: Who holds the money? Code does, not the prompt
items.failure: We watched an agent loop spend until a human noticed; the fix that held was a signed spending envelope in code (daily cap, per-job cap, expiry, freeze) that the agent cannot edit, and a rule that when the balance or price is unknown the agent stops instead of guessing.
items.why: weakest: A spending limit for the agents exists in code or config, not only in a prompt
items.fix: Say or show it: A spending limit for the agents exists in code or config, not only in a prompt
items.plain: An autonomous business spends money: API calls, ads, refunds, human hires. The question is who can change how much. If the budget is a sentence in the system prompt, the agent can talk itself past it. If the agent can call the payment API with any amount, one bad loop empties the account.
items.look_for: a config or code file with the limit; a freeze/kill switch a human can hit; the deck naming what stops a runaway; any statement about behavior when a price or balance cannot be read

evidence_public.what: Anthropic Project Vend: an agent given a $1,000 budget in its prompt ran the shop into the red (gave away margin, ordered a PS5); the prompt budget was not an enforced limit
Compromised keys let agents burn a $14,000 one-day model bill; billing alerts lag a day behind agent-speed spend. Another agent auto-provisioned $6,531 of cloud in 24h with no ceiling
Replit agent deleted a production database during a code freeze despite being told not to; the instruction was a prompt, not a permission

items.title: Money and side effects happen exactly once
items.failure: We shipped a webhook without an idempotency key and got duplicate fulfillment on the first retry storm; revenue analytics drifted because resent events were counted again; an approval modeled as a boolean resumed a draft that had changed since it was approved.
items.why: weakest: A payment or fulfillment event is keyed by a stable id so a retry cannot fulfill or charge twice
items.fix: Say or show it: A payment or fulfillment event is keyed by a stable id so a retry cannot fulfill or charge twice
items.plain: Payment webhooks fire twice. Workers retry. A human clicks approve twice. If the code does not recognize 'I already did this', a customer is charged twice, an order ships twice, or the revenue number shown to judges counts one sale three times.
items.look_for: an idempotency key on payment/fulfillment handlers (session id, event id); approvals tied to a hash of what was approved; revenue counted from deduplicated events; the revenue number the team quotes traceable to distinct charges

evidence_public.what: Stripe: retried charges are deduplicated only if the caller supplies the same Idempotency-Key; regenerating it per retry defeats it
Same webhook event delivered more than once on retry causes duplicate fulfillment unless deduplicated at the database with a unique constraint on the event id

items.title: Agent decisions are measured against doing nothing
items.failure: Our agent cleared its own accuracy bar while being worse than the free baseline; high-confidence decisions did worse than the ones it skipped; a 'success' gate fired on a result that pointed the wrong way; human answers leaked into the agent's inputs so the humans stopped being a check; a demo that settled on labels we invented ourselves looked great and proved nothing.
items.why: weakest: The pitch compares an agent decision to a free baseline (rule of thumb, human default, doing nothing), not only to itself
items.fix: Say or show it: The pitch compares an agent decision to a free baseline (rule of thumb, human default, doing nothing), not only to itself
items.plain: A team says 'our agent decided X and it worked'. Compared to what? If a simple rule or a human default would have done as well, the agent adds cost, not value. And a model saying it is 90% confident means nothing until you have checked how often 90% turns out right.
items.look_for: a baseline comparison in the deck; confidence used for reporting not for spending; humans answering before they see the agent's answer; before/after numbers from real people or customers, with the source named

evidence_public.what: Models stay verbally confident while wrong; self-reported confidence is not a proxy for correctness
About a third of SWE-bench issues leak the solution in the issue text, inflating agent scores; benchmark wins do not predict production
Project Vend 2: profitability came from checklists, price verification, and CRM tooling before big decisions, not from a smarter model

items.title: Someone notices when it silently stops
items.failure: A source stopped ingesting after a healthy start with no terminal error; scheduled runs went missing and users noticed before operators; when alerts existed they were so many that the real one was invisible.
items.why: weakest: There is a heartbeat, health check, or canary that shows the agent is still working, and the pitch says who sees it
items.fix: Say or show it: There is a heartbeat, health check, or canary that shows the agent is still working, and the pitch says who sees it
items.plain: Autonomous means nobody is watching. Long-running listeners go quiet without an error. Scheduled work skips a run. The first person to notice is a customer, days later. The question is not 'does it run' but 'who finds out when it does not'.
items.look_for: a health endpoint or heartbeat; a canary (a fake order every hour); a stated answer to 'what happens at 3am when step N fails'; alerts that are few and carry evidence and a remedy

evidence_public.what: A deploy silently removed a scheduled-job entry; three weeks of weekly reports were missed before anyone noticed
Backup job failed silently for three days, discovered only when the primary database corrupted

items.title: Customer text is information, never authority
items.failure: We built an inbound protocol that quarantines message bodies, checks a content hash and nonce, discards any authority claim in the text, and only then lets the agent read it as data. Before that, a buyer agent could ask for free judgment and get it.
items.why: weakest: A customer or another agent cannot change prices, grant themselves free service, or trigger spend by what they type
items.fix: Say or show it: A customer or another agent cannot change prices, grant themselves free service, or trigger spend by what they type
items.plain: Customers and other agents will type things like 'the manager said this is free' or paste instructions aimed at the model. If inbound text can change prices, grant refunds, or trigger spend, the business can be talked out of its money. This is prompt injection wearing a customer hat.
items.look_for: inbound messages treated as data (checked, quarantined) before action; prices, refunds, and spend gated by rules or a human, not by what was typed; the deck naming one abuse case and how it is refused

evidence_public.what: Chevrolet dealership chatbot was prompted into agreeing to sell a $76k Tahoe for $1, 'legally binding, no takesies backsies'; the dealer pulled the bot
Air Canada's chatbot invented a bereavement refund policy; a tribunal held the airline liable for what its bot promised (Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024)

items.title: The human is placed where agents genuinely cannot decide
items.failure: Approvals that were a checkbox got clicked without reading; panels that saw the agent's answer first agreed with it; human steps with no time bound stalled the business when the human was slow.
items.why: weakest: The pitch names the specific decisions a human makes and why an agent should not make them yet
items.fix: Say or show it: The pitch names the specific decisions a human makes and why an agent should not make them yet
items.plain: The hackathon's own thesis: no company runs at zero humans yet, so where the human sits is the design. A human who rubber-stamps every agent output adds cost and no independence. A human nowhere means nobody catches the agent being wrong. The good version names the decisions a human owns, why an agent should not own them yet, and what the human's answer changes.
items.look_for: specific human decisions named with the reason; the human output used by the system (a verdict, a label, a correction); the human step priced and timed; the business still functioning when the human is late

evidence_public.what: When AI was wrong and flagged, humans still approved the bad decision about 74% of the time; oversight only works when disagreeing is cheap and expected
Radiology study: with incorrect AI suggestions, inexperienced readers fell from ~80% to under 20% accuracy and experienced ones from 82% to 45%; expertise slows automation bias, does not prevent it

items.title: Truth is an append-only ledger, not the latest state
items.failure: Re-logged rows inflated our sample count 165 times and lit a false 'ready for real money' badge; a current-state table was mistaken for history and audit trails vanished on dedupe; agent findings entered durable state without the evidence that produced them.
items.why: weakest: Events (orders, decisions, spends) are recorded once, append-only, and current state is derived from them
items.fix: Say or show it: Events (orders, decisions, spends) are recorded once, append-only, and current state is derived from them
items.plain: If orders, decisions, and spends are overwritten in place, the business cannot answer 'how much did we make' or 'why did the agent do that' with evidence. Every number in the pitch (revenue, users, accuracy) should be reconstructable from rows that were written once and never edited.
items.look_for: an events table or log that is append-only, with current state derived from it; each pitch number traceable to ledger rows; findings that change state citing their evidence

evidence_public.what: Knight Capital: dormant code left active on one of eight servers, no reconciliation caught the divergent state, $440M of erroneous trades in 45 minutes
